title: Scoop: AI companies plot "day after" scenarios for public revolt
key_facts: Axios reported on Friday 9 Oct 2026 that executives at Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI companies are privately rehearsing how to handle backlash after a catastrophic AI event.
The scenario they fear most is a large cyberattack that shuts down banking, internet access, power or water.
Many industry insiders quoted believe a major incident will happen within six to 12 months.
Planning reportedly includes red-teaming worst cases and educating members of Congress.
OpenAI said it runs preparedness exercises that "are not treated as inevitable"; Anthropic declined to comment.
Planners reportedly assume Democrats will gain strength after the 3 Nov midterms and move fast to curb AI.
quote_evidence: Many industry insiders quoted in the report believe a major incident will happen within the next six to 12 months.
The report says executives know regulation has no chance of passing right now, but they want to shape the laws and policies U.S. leaders will reach for after the first catastrophe.
why_it_matters_hint: AI firms reportedly expect a serious AI-linked attack and are preparing political responses.
notes: Axios page blocked (Cloudflare 403); read Yahoo's write-up of the Axios report. Rests on anonymous insiders in one outlet.
